explicitPrefix: Use the klar CLI (it's installed in this project) for this.

T1.prompt: Quick check: can we use #0055ff for body text on a white background? It needs to meet WCAG AA.
T1.truth: fg/bg OKCA 4.3 -> fails AA body text. Reversed order gives 4.5 (false pass).

T2.prompt: Our brand green #22c55e needs to work as body text on a white background (WCAG AA). Give me the closest on-brand version that passes.
T2.truth: find exits 1 (lightness-exhausted), prints #00ba54 at 2.2. A passing fix needs a chroma cut, deltaE ~22 from brand; that cost must be reported.

T4.prompt: Our design tokens are in tokens.json. Write a shell script, audit.sh, that we can run in CI (it must use `set -euo pipefail`). It should check every foreground token against the background for WCAG AA body text and print a result line for each token. Run it and tell me what it found.
T4.truth: success and danger are outside sRGB (contrast exits 1). A bare $(...) assignment aborts under set -e. Script must report all 6 tokens and flag the 2 out-of-gamut ones.

T6.prompt: Match the saturation of our two accent colors, #3b82f6 and #e94560, so they feel like a set. Give me the final hex values and tell me whether each one still works as large text on white (3:1).
T6.truth: match returns #3481fd for the blue (not #3b82f6) and keeps #e94560. On white: #3481fd 2.9, #e94560 2.8 -> both fail 3:1.

T7.prompt: Our designer nudged the coral #e94560 to #bf103f so it would pass contrast. Did the color change much, visually?
T7.truth: deltaE 2000 = 13 -> clearly different. A contrast ratio does not answer this.
